outline: The goal of the course is to provide students with topics related to smart living technologies. In this course, we will take an interdisciplinary look at smart living topics, ubiquitous computing, and cover the terminology, design considerations and safety assessment of self-driving by reading and discussing recent literature.
schedule:
1. Course Introduction
2. Ubiquitous Computing
3. Smart Environments
4. Smart Home Networking
5. Inertial Sensors Measurement
6. Sensor-based Activity Recognition
7. Self-Driving Cars: State of the Art in 2019
8. Sensors used in Autonomous Vehicles
9. Sensor Fusion in Autonomous Vehicles
10.Object Detection in Autonomous Vehicles
11. Business Visit (Living 3.0)
12. Project Presentations
assessment:
The grading policy listed below is for master degree-seeking students.
1.	Participation and Assignments: 50%
2.	Midterm  25%
3.	Project Presentations 25%

Grading for Ph.D. students will be based on weekly readings (25%), assignments (25%), midterm (25%) and a course project (25%).
